entries.reason: CSRF origin verification now recognizes a verified tenant domain as same-site (multi-tenant #20, follow-up to PR #422 review). verifyCsrfOrigin compared Origin against NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL alone, so a browser on a bound white-label domain sent that domain and every mutation returned 403 while reads resolved normally. The allowance is deliberately narrower than accepting any bound tenant domain: the Origin must name the host the request was actually addressed to, and that host must be present in platform_tenant_domains. Accepting any bound domain would let a page on one tenant mint state-changing requests against another, a cross-tenant CSRF vector that does not exist while the allow-list is a single origin; a dedicated adversarial case pins it closed. The Origin must also be a bare serialized origin, because URL parsing silently discards userinfo and the first version accepted https://user@<bound-host> until the adversarial case caught it, and must be https in production. The original single-origin comparison is unchanged and still decides first, so no request on the platform domain reaches the new path or pays for it. Each of these operations changes only its sourceHash, from awaiting the now-async call; no control, classification, principalSource or tenantSource changed on any of them, verified by comparison against the effective manifest.
